newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP socialists criticise EMU budget pact.
newsitem.headline: EP socialists criticise EMU budget pact.

text.p: European Parliament socialists on Tuesday launched a blistering attack on the EU's agreed stability and growth pact for countries joining monetary union.

At a meeting of the parliament's monetary sub-committee, several MEPs criticised Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm's claim that they had been properly consulted on the details of a pact that would fine governments with excessive deficits.

"If you think that I am prepared to vote in favour of this so that you can add it to the trophies on the Dutch presidency's mantlepiece, you can forget it," said Alan Donnelly, socialist spokesman on economic policy.
Donnelly and others accused EU finance ministers of sidestepping democratic control over economic policy by handing crucial powers to a committee of bureacrats.

But Zalm, bewildered at the level of discontent over the pact, calmly reassured the committee that recent decisions by EU finance ministers had only fleshed out what in principle what was agreed by all 15 member states.
"All we've done is transpose the Dublin accord into a more formal text," Zalm said, referring to the political agreement reached at the Dublin summit of EU leaders in December.
"If I'm not mistaken, the drafting of this is nothing new. I can't see how we've diverged from Dublin," he added.
EU finance ministers resolved several technical issues on how governments would be fined when they met in Noordwijk for an informal session several weeks ago.
The MEPs were also critical of the Commission, which they said had shed some of its responsibilities for oversight of economic policies in the EU.
Commission officials, however, played down the row over the budget pact, saying the parliament's primary concern was over procedural issues and not the substance of the accord.
"They want to make a political point in terms of procedure," said one Commission official.
